text: Yellow pigmentation of mature foxtail millet kernels is a quality trait. Genome-wide association analysis identified genomic regions associated with yellow pigment content, lutein and zeaxanthin. SiPSY1 (Phytoene synthase 1) was confirmed as the main contributor to all three components by knockout and overexpression analysis.

Sorghum's drought stress resistance must be genetically enhanced. Research has been conducted on drought tolerance traits such as stay green and grain production. Novel drought-related traits such as canopy temperature, stomatal conductance, reflectance indices, and chlorophyll fluorescence must be investigated and employed in breeding.

Subsets of multiple sorghum populations, including the Sorghum Association Panel (SAP), the Sorghum Mini Core Collection and the Senegalese sorghum population, have been screened against sorghum diseases anthracnose, downy mildew, grain mold and head smut. These studies were performed in a univariate framework.

Foxtail millet has a drought response network involving root system remodeling, stomatal regulation, osmotic adjustment, photosynthetic and metabolic reprogramming. Signaling modules involving Ca-2+, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and abscisic acid (ABA) coordinate these processes. Transcription factors (TFs), non-coding RNAs, and epigenetic modifications fine-tune the network.

Expression profiling indicated VfAP2/ERFs were expressed during growth and development, and were responsive to drought and salt stresses. RT-qPCR revealed six VfAP2/ERF genes were upregulated under drought and salt stress.
Stable QTL were identified across seasons. Of the 60 mapped genic markers, 21 were at QTL peaks or tightly linked to QTL.

The Pc98 gene was mapped using F-2:3 populations from crosses Pc98/Bingo and Pc98/Kasztan. Pc98 is a single-gene line carrying Pc98. Both populations were evaluated in seedling inoculation experiments.

Eighty-one SSR primer pairs from chromosome 6D were tested. Five were polymorphic in the two parents and two contrasting bulks, confirming the 6D location of Dw6. Using these five polymorphic markers, Dw6 was mapped to a 1.0 cM interval flanked by markers SSR83 and SSR120.

We validated tightly linked markers in 23 diverse sorghum accessions by genotyping and phenotyping for germination stimulant activity towards S. asiatica and S. hermonthica. The markers co-segregated with Striga germination stimulant activity in 21 of the 23 lines.

Seven genes enhance drought tolerance via signalling pathways such as CDPK and MSBP, anti-senescence via GDA2, and detoxification via GST. Additionally, 18 genes including P5CS, PP2C, and chaperones were differentially expressed in all genotypes under drought, indicating they are general drought-responsive genes in barley.
Sihc1 was narrowed to a 354.84 kb region containing 30 open reading frames. Seita.6G226500, Seita.6G226800, Seita.6G228300, and Seita.6G228600 are key candidates for Sihc1.

Diagnostic molecular markers were developed to distinguish 12 known alleles of barley VRN1 (HvVRN1), including a new allele. The new allele, HvVRN1-11, has a 3172-bp deletion in Intron I of HvVRN1 and was identified in a Chinese barley landrace.

Differentially expressed genes were transcriptionally up-regulated under heat and drought stress. These genes were enriched in the oxylipin biosynthetic process and proline biosynthetic process. Genes were transcriptionally down-regulated under heat and drought stress. These down-regulated genes were enriched in the thiamine metabolic process and calcium sensing receptor.

Two hundred and seventy-seven F-2 progeny and their F-2:3 families from a cross between Westland A line (susceptible parent) and PI550610 (resistant parent) were used with 118 polymorphic SSR markers to map greenbug resistance QTLs. Composite interval mapping and multiple interval mapping revealed two QTLs on sorghum chromosome nine (SBI-09) that conditioned resistance to greenbug. The QTLs were designated QSsgr-09-01 (major) and QSsgr-09-02 (minor), accounting for approximately 55-80% and 1-6% of the phenotypic variation for resistance to greenbug feeding, respectively.

This study investigated the water absorption capacity of 300 foxtail millet germplasm resources. It identified two candidate genes, Si4g02810 and Si4g02840, associated with saturated water absorption through GWAS. The genes are hypothesized to function in starch synthesis.

The AP2/ERF family gene SbERF027 is a novel regulator of cold tolerance. SbERF027 expression is high in seedlings and panicles and is induced by low temperature. The cold-induced expression level of SbERF027 is higher in cold-tolerant accession SZ7 than in cold-sensitive accession Z-5. SbERF027 is detected in the nucleus under normal and cold stress conditions.

34 of the 159 QTL were identified in 2 to 12 environments. 88 QTL controlling different traits formed 34 co-located QTL clusters. The triple QTL cluster qPD9.2/qPL9.5/qPEL9.3 was detected 23 times in 13 environments.
SbSNAC1 is a NAC transcription factor involved in abiotic stress response in sorghum. It has a typical NAC conserved domain at the N terminus and a diverse C-terminal region.

Five converted markers amplified expected products in resistant bulks. Three of them segregated according to resistance in the whole population and showed a high correlation coefficient between marker and phenotype. The PCR-based converted markers could be used for identification of the Pm4 gene in oat.

Seed dormancy in wild mungbean may be useful for breeding cultivated mungbean with pre-harvest sprouting resistance. Two major QTLs for seed dormancy, HsA and Sdwa5.1.1+, were identified in wild mungbean and may share the same locus or be linked.

Powdery mildew is caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. hordei. 106 RIL lines were derived from a cross between Badia and Kavir. The study used these lines to identify and validate QTLs associated with powdery mildew resistance at seedling and adult stages under control, drought, and saline conditions.

Foxtail millet is a model genetic system for studying traits such as architectural evolution, C-4 photosynthesis, nutritional properties, abiotic tolerance and bioenergy. Excavating QTLs of yield component traits facilitates genetic research in foxtail millet and close cereal species.

BMX-010015 was stable across environments based on yield traits and grain yield. BMX-08010-2 showed a regression coefficient (bi) greater than unity and non-significant deviation from regression (S(2)di) values, indicating suitability for favorable environments.

Stem rust is a disease of cultivated oat (Avena sativa) caused by Puccinia graminis f. sp. avenae. Host resistance is the primary control strategy and is conferred by a small number of resistance genes.

The expression of the foxtail millet R2R3-MYB factor SiMYB16 is induced by salt and drought. SiMYB16 is localized in the nucleus and acts as a transcriptional activator. SiMYB16 belongs to the R2R3-MYB transcription factor family subgroup 24.

The oat variety 'Firth', and related varieties 'Husky' and 'Flämingstip', contain an APR gene. This gene was previously located on chromosome 1D using DArT markers. The study aimed to confirm and refine its location, tentatively named Pm13.

HSF transcription factors mediate the stress response. The study provides theoretical references for understanding quinoa's response to high temperature stress, and for screening high temperature tolerant genes and strains. The findings reveal regulation of the HSF transcription factor family in response to high temperature stress to improve quinoa varieties.
Four QTLs for ECL were identified on chromosomes 2, 7, 10 and 11. InDel mapping detected QTLs qECL7.1 on chromosome 7 and qECL10.1 on chromosome 10.

A collection of 334 worldwide two-rowed barley accessions was evaluated for grain size traits: grain length (GL), grain width (GW), and thousand-grain weight (TGW) across six field trials. Significant differences were observed in genotype and environments. SNP- and InDel-based GWAS were applied to dissect the genetic architecture of grain size using an SLAF-seq strategy.
Seven agronomic traits of 408 diverse foxtail millet accessions were evaluated in three environments. They were clustered into two divergent groups based on genotypic data.
Distal intergenomic translocations predominated from the C- to the D-genome chromosomes. Translocations from A- to C-, or D- to C-genome chromosomes were less frequent.
Two major QTLs, Qsd1 and Qsd2, control seed dormancy in barley. Two KASP markers were developed and applied in a genotypic survey of 859 cultivated barley accessions.

VfbZIP5 overexpression in plants resulted in lower proline, malondialdehyde and peroxidase levels under drought stress compared to empty vector control. Protein-protein interaction analysis showed VfbZIP5 interacted with seven proteins in faba bean, including VfbZIP7 and VfbZIP10.

To evaluate genetic diversity and identify molecular markers for starch content in barley, 40 cultivated barley genotypes were used. These genotypes included those with high or low starch content. All genotypes were re-sequenced using double-digest-restriction associated DNA sequencing, yielding 299,103 SNP markers. The genotypes were divided into four sub-populations based on FASTSTRUCTURE, principal component analysis and neighbour-joining tree analysis.

Annual ryegrass had a higher recovery percentage than perennial ryegrass under stress. Salinity stress and alkalinity stress are different. The salt-alkaline tolerance of ryegrass seeds is affected by the interactions of temperature and salinity-alkalinity.
A QTL (QSRL(IV_61.63)) associated with specific root length was identified near TP1873 and flanked by F7XEM6b SRAP marker and TP1035 SNP marker. These two QTLs were detected in both seasons.

This study identifies and maps QTLs for resistance to cowpea bruchids. 120 F-2 lines from a cross between MU9 (susceptible) and WC42 (resistant) were genotyped with 2753 SNP markers. F-2:3 seeds were screened for bruchid resistance.
The ASM produced a 261 bp fragment in tolerant accessions and no amplification in sensitive accessions. This ASM enables marker-aided breeding of foxtail millet for dehydration tolerance.

Short straw is a desired trait in cultivated hexaploid oat (Avena sativa L.). Marker-assisted selection is limited by a lack of mapping data and available markers. Bulked-segregant analysis identified PCR-based markers associated with a dwarfing gene.

We identified 288 putative transcription factors (TFs) involved in drought response. The WRKY, NAC, AP2/ERF, bHLH, bZIP, and MYB families were enriched and might play crucial roles in drought stress response of sheepgrass.
Six major QTLs were identified under salt stress. Positive effects were from Shihong137, except for qRL10-2.

A recombinant inbred line (RIL) population was derived from Tx642 and Tx7000. Phenotypic data were collected in three field trials and one greenhouse trial. High TD corresponded to high WL. The r(2) of TD against WL was highest under non-stress greenhouse conditions. It was larger in cooler, irrigated field conditions than in hotter, drier field trials.

JQ-00084 is a genotype with a yield > 3000 kg ha(-1), a 1000-grain weight exceeding 2 g, and a flowering-to-maturity period over 80 days. JQ-00315, JQ-00521, JQ-1029, and JQ-02405 fulfilled at least four criteria.
RNA-seq and qRT-PCR results show that SiNLP2 responds to low-nitrogen stress. SiNLP2 regulates the expression of SiNAR2.1A, SiNAR2.1B, SiNRT1.1, and SiNR2 genes in nitrogen pathways.
67 candidate genes responsive to abiotic stresses were co-located with the abiotic-stress MQTL. 55 of these genes had different conserved motifs.

Six CIPKs showed leaf-specific expression under normal conditions, linking leaf function regulation to alkali stress responses in sweet sorghum. Yeast two-hybrid assay demonstrated specific interactions between multiple SbCIPKs and SbCBLs.

Pc98 co-segregated with four SNP markers in the Pc98/Kasztan population. The closest flanking markers were GMI_DS_LB_6017_kom367 and avgbs2_153634.1.59_kom410 with genetic distances of 0.7 cM and 0.3 cM, respectively. Two SNP loci defined a haplotype that accurately predicted Pc98 status in oat germplasm. This haplotype is valuable for marker-assisted selection of Pc98 in oat breeding.

Three QTL clusters (Cluster-1-Ah03, Cluster-2-Ah12, Cluster-3-Ah20) harbor major QTLs for heat tolerant traits. Important candidate genes are underlying these clusters: DHHC-type zinc finger family protein (arahy.J0Y6Y5), peptide transporter 1 (arahy.8ZMT0C), pentatricopeptide repeat-containing protein (arahy.4A4JE9), Ulp1 protease family (arahy.X568GS), Kelch repeat F-box protein (arahy.I7X4PC), FRIGIDA-like protein (arahy.0C3V8Z), and post-illumination chlorophyll fluorescence increase (arahy.92ZGJC). Their putative functions involve seed development, plant architecture regulation, yield, genesis and growth, flowering time regulation, and photosynthesis.

Quinoa seedlings of 'NL-6' were treated with water, NaCl, and NaCl with ACC. They were analyzed by transcriptional sequencing and TMT quantitative proteomics to reveal ethylene involvement in quinoa responses to salt stress.

Overexpression of VaERF3 in transgenic Arabidopsis increased proline accumulation and decreased malondialdehyde and reactive oxygen species under saline-alkaline stress. VaERF3 encodes a nuclear-localized transcriptional activator that promotes stress-responsive gene expression.

A genome-wide association study investigated the genetic basis of nutraceutical traits in buckwheat. It evaluated 10 traits: phenol, flavonoids, antioxidants, methionine, lysine, protein content, nitrogen, iron, zinc, and ascorbic acid, using 132 diverse genotypes.

Genome duplication resulted in more drought-related genes and higher expression levels in autopolyploid than in diploid. 186 drought-related genes were differentially expressed, with 97 up-regulated in DiH826Dr_vs_DiH826Ck. 297 drought-related genes were differentially expressed, with 126 up-regulated in TetraH832Dr_vs_TetraH832Ck. Among these, 81 genes were specific to DiH826Dr_vs_DiH826Ck, and 192 genes were specific to TetraH832Dr_vs_TetraH832Ck.
One gene, Seita.9G321800, encoded MYBS3 transcription factor and upregulated after drought stress. It is homologous with MYBS3 in maize, rice, and sorghum and named SiMYBS3.

Salt tolerance was evaluated for 100 oat cultivars. Two salt-tolerant cultivars and two salt-sensitive cultivars were used to compare physiological responses and expression patterns of Na+- and K+-transport-related genes under salinity.

AsCDPK promoters contain cis-acting elements for hormones, biotic and abiotic stresses. AsCDPK gene expression is induced by salt stresses, showing stress-specific responses. Overexpression of AsCDPK26 gene enhances salt resistance in C. reinhardtii.

AsA priming repaired structural damage in aged seeds, with intact double membranes and clear internal cristae observed in mitochondria. AsA priming reduced H2O2 levels in mitochondria of aged seeds by increasing the activities of CAT, GR, MDHAR and DHAR.

Two loci affected seedling infection type to TGN and adult field reactions. Two other loci were restricted to adult plants. Additional loci on chromosomes 1D and 6D contributed to adult plant field resistance.

The tan1-d allele has a 12-bp deletion at position 659 nt in Tannin1. The tan1-e allele has a 10-bp deletion at position 771 nt in Tannin1. The tan2-d allele contains a C-to-T transition, resulting in a premature stop codon before the bHLH domain in Tannin2.

Overexpression of SbWRKY51 via Agrobacterium rhizogenes-mediated hairy root transformation enhanced salt tolerance in sorghum. It resulted in longer root length, increased biomass, less Na+ content, and higher antioxidant enzyme activities compared to wild-type plants. Ectopic expression of SbWRKY51 in Arabidopsis showed similar phenotypes. Mutation of the homologous gene AtWRKY11 increased salt sensitivity in Arabidopsis.
Five major QTLs for SDW_70 were stable across locations. Candidate genes with SNPs and AhMITE1 insertion were identified for the major QTL regions.
HvASRs have a typical ABA/WDS domain and similar motif arrangements. Two tandem duplicate gene pairs, HvASR4/5/6/7 and HvASR8/9, were identified.

Association analysis used 181 SSR markers and nine phenotypic traits from a structured sorghum population of 96 accessions evaluated under optimum and drought stressed conditions. Genomic regions associated with major drought tolerance QTLs were annotated with NCBI and sorghum databases to identify drought responsive genes, which were transcriptionally analyzed.
The QTL-seq study identified a SNP marker (Chr6: 2686447C>G) validated on a diverse panel. This marker can be used in molecular marker-assisted selection to improve aphid resistance in sorghum.
SiLEA14 was induced by osmotic stress, NaCl and abscisic acid. SiLEA14 protein localized in nucleus and cytoplasm.

Deadheart percentage had low heritability and high environmental influence, indicating shoot fly resistance is a complex trait requiring marker assisted selection. Transgressive variation for all traits in the RIL population indicated alleles for resistance contributed from both resistant and susceptible parents.

This study evaluated phenotypic variation and identified SRAP molecular markers for 144 oat germplasm accessions. Substantial phenotypic diversity was observed, with coefficients of variation exceeding 20% for key traits including beta-glucan content, crude fat content, main panicle components, and yield.

The sucrose metabolism pathway plays a role in salt response in foxtail millet. It provides UDP-glucose for cellulose synthesis and energy production, and promotes flavonoid synthesis to enhance salt tolerance. Over-expressing the phospho-mimic sucrose synthase (SuS) (SuS(S10D)) in soybean roots enhanced salt tolerance compared to over-expressing SuS lines.

Genotyping of parents and selected lines from two hybrid populations, and SNP positions on chromosomes with haplotypes, were confirmed by DArT microarray analysis. Differential expression profiles were identified in parents and hybrids under gradual drought and rapid dehydration.

In NGS-based bulked segregation analysis, using 920,389 genome-wide markers, four QTLs (qtlMs-6.1, qtlMs-6.2, qtlMs-6.3, qtlMs-6.4) were identified on chromosome 6. Comparative transcriptome analysis identified 245 differentially expressed genes (190 upregulated, 55 downregulated) in resistant 407B and 576 differentially expressed genes (336 upregulated, 240 downregulated) in susceptible 7B at 4 dpi.

Genes near significant markers on chromosomes 3A and 2C have functions related to stress tolerance and cellular processes. These results identify genomic regions controlling TKW in subtropical environments for oat breeding.

The study investigated quinoa salt tolerance at an early developmental stage and grain nutritional value. Genotypes showed significant variability in salt response attributes at the first development stage, including Amarilla Sacaca (A.
A recombinant inbred line population from a cross between 'KS115' and 'Macia' was evaluated in two locations. A genetic map used 112 molecular markers including nine carotenoid candidate genes.

SbNAC9 overexpression in sorghum seedlings enhanced drought-stress tolerance. It increased chlorophyll content, PSII photochemical efficiency, root system strength, and ROS scavenging capability compared to wild-type.
Sorghum lines were assessed for reactive oxygen species production induced by flg22 treatment. Flg22-induced ROS production varied consistently between lines.

Genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS)-derived molecular markers reveal distinct genetic population structure and narrow genetic diversity of Chinese hulless oat landraces. Genome-wide association study (GWAS) identifies four markers linked to the naked grain gene (N1).

Resistance differed between the two parental lines and among their F-2 progeny in response to greenbug feeding at 7, 10, 14 and 21 days after infestation. A linkage map of 729.5 cM was constructed with 102 polymorphic SSR markers (69 genomic and 33 EST SSRs).

Joint analyses across borer species and sites revealed 4 QTLs controlling deadheart formation; 6 QTLs controlling leaf feeding damage; 5 QTLs controlling exit holes and stem tunneling damages; 2 QTLs controlling bloom waxiness, leaf glossiness, and seedling vigour; 4 QTLs conditioning trichome density; and 6 QTLs conditioning leaf toughness. Joint analyses for B. fusca and C. partellus revealed that marker CS132-2 colocalised for leaf toughness and stem tunneling traits on QTLs 1 and 2, respectively. This study recommended further studies to identify genes underlying the mapped QTLs.

A QTL controlling seedling growth under one abiotic stress can respond to another stress. QTL promoting faster growth under non-stress conditions were also identified under salt and osmotic stresses. These loci can be exploited in breeding programs.

Rphq2 is a minor gene for partial resistance to Puccinia hordei. It was physically mapped in a 188 kbp introgression with suppressed recombination between haplotypes of rphq2 and Rphq2 barley cultivars. Partial and non-host resistances to rust fungi in barley may be based on PAMP-triggered immunity.

Allele analysis indicated that linked SNPs differentiate tan from red/purple accessions, but not red from purple. The candidate genes and SNP markers may facilitate plant color development elucidation and molecular plant breeding.

The PYL4-ABA complex was the most stable, with a binding energy of -6.8 kcal/mol. This indicates the PYL module is involved in the ABA signal transduction pathway, which is crucial for stress-responsive gene expression.
The loss of DRNL function affects gynoecium development. The mutant phenotypes are similar to those in plants treated with exogenous cytokinins. AHP6 is a target of DRNL.

Mutation of the homologous gene AtWRKY55 in A. thaliana enhanced salt tolerance. SbWRKY55 supplementation restored salt tolerance in the mutants. In transgenic sorghum with SbWRKY55 overexpression, expression levels of genes in the abscisic acid (ABA) pathway were altered and endogenous ABA content decreased.

New SSR markers were developed from 'Kanota' and 'Ogle' genomic DNA libraries. The objectives were to increase SSR markers on the 'Fulghum' x 'Norline' recombinant inbred population genetic map and to scan for QTL associated with winter field survival, crown freezing tolerance, vernalization response, and heading date.

BLASTP annotation of QTL genomic sequences identified 86 gene homologs. Fifteen of these genes are drought responsive. All fifteen genes were differentially expressed in drought tolerant and susceptible accessions. Their expression levels were highly induced by drought stress.

Six yield-related traits were analyzed for 214 sorghum germplasm. 2,811,016 SNPs markers were produced by resequencing. After controlling Q and K, QTLs were found to be related to the traits using three algorithms.

Drought stress increased citrulline content in leaves and stems up to 38-fold and 16-fold, respectively. Amino acid correlation indicated activation of a metabolic pathway involving citrulline, its precursor ornithine, and catabolic product arginine.

Drought stress affects the panicle of foxtail millet at the yield formation stage. The study examined panicle morphology, photosynthesis, antioxidant enzymes, reactive oxygen species, osmotic regulation, and RNA-seq in leaves under light drought stress (LD), heavy drought stress (HD), light drought control (LDCK), and heavy drought control (HDCK).
Photoperiod-sensitive flowering is a key adaptive trait for sorghum. An association analysis investigated the effect of polymorphisms in genes on photoperiod-sensitive flowering time in sorghum.

Applying a mixed model approach to candidate genes, we found significant associations between several SNPs with PRI for the genes CRYPTOCHROME 1 (CRY1-b1) and GIGANTEA (GI). Tajima's D negative values for the genes suggested purifying selection has acted on genes involved in photoperiodic control of flowering time in sorghum.

The hybrid sorghum exhibited high-parent heterosis for net photosynthetic rate (P-n), transpiration rate (T-r), stomatal conductance (G(s)), apparent leaf meat conductance (AMC), ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase, phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, and sucrose phosphate synthase. Intercellular CO2 concentration (C-i), instantaneous water use efficiency (WUE), and sucrose synthase showed negative heterosis.
CcCIPK13 and CcCIPK14 overexpression increased survival rates after drought. Genistin, genistein and apigenin were upregulated.

Significant marker-trait associations were identified for nodal root angle on chromosomes 1, 3, 6, and 7. The SNP loci with the highest phenotypic variance explanation (PVE) are: sbi32853830 (PVE=18.2%) for NNR, sbi29954292 (PVE=18.1%) for LA, sbi24668980 (PVE=10.8%) for SDW, sbi3022983 (PVE=7%) for NRA, sbi29897704 (PVE=6.4%) for NRL, and sbi29897694 (PVE=5.3%) for SFW.

We identified 27 germplasm resources suitable for high-yield foxtail millet breeding. Through haplotype and phenotype association analysis, we pinpointed the gene SiTGW6, which governs grain yield in foxtail millet.

Greenbug (Schizaphis graminum) is a major insect pest of sorghum, causing serious damage. Identification of chromosomal regions for greenbug resistance facilitates map-based cloning and marker-assisted breeding. A mapping experiment was conducted to dissect sorghum genetic resistance to greenbug biotype I into genomic regions.

Two Sorghum bicolor genotypes, RTx430 and BTx642, with differing preflowering drought tolerances, were grown under water limitation for 8 weeks. Their leaf cytosolic- and organelle-enriched protein profiles were compared. Drought induced significant changes in the abundance of multiple heat shock proteins and dehydrins in both genotypes.

F5 and F6 populations were constructed with XL52 and W452 as parents to verify QTLs. A significant correlation was found between the juice yield trait and the Xtxp97 marker. Based on progeny tests of 29 recombinants, QJy-sbi06 was located in a 21.2 kb region on chromosome 6. A candidate gene encoding an NAC transcription factor (sobic.006G147400) was identified in that region.

Three algorithms, FGENESH, GENSCAN and GENMARK, predicted five genes (NSP, NAD, PHD, MADS, MLO) in QTL qSTG1A on chromosome 3, ten genes (IAA, SORBIDRAFT, CYP450, GAG/POL, PK, GENE X, UGTS, MTC, AGP16, VP25) in QTL qSTG2 on chromosome 1, and one gene (SF CC1) in QTL qSTG3 on chromosome 1. Structural features and protein annotations indicated their involvement in drought tolerance pathways.

QTL for grain width and hundred-grain weight were detected near markers SWU_Fe_InDe1086 and SWU_Fe_InDe1076. Candidate genes with expression or InDel differences between parents were screened within the QTL interval.

RFLP probe sequences were evaluated for simple sequence repeats (SSRs). 60 SSRs were developed and assayed in sorghum germplasm including inbreds, landraces and wild relatives. These SSR loci had lower polymorphism (D=0.46) compared to SSRs isolated by library hybridization screens (D=0.69).
Pc45 and PcKM mapped to the same location on Mrg08 (chromosome 12D). This suggests Pc45 and PcKM are the same resistance gene, but allelism or tight linkage cannot be ruled out.

Abiotic stresses from climate change cause agricultural losses. These stresses include water scarcity, extreme temperatures, high irradiance, saline soils, nutrient deprivation and heavy metal contamination. They compromise crop development and productivity.

SbNAC2 overexpression in Arabidopsis and rice induces antioxidant enzyme activity under abiotic stress. SbNAC2 directly activates the expression of the stress responsive AP2/ERF type TF gene SbAP37 by binding to the TTNCGTA motif of its promoter.

Haplotype analysis identified 8 distinct haplotypes in candidate genes associated with drought stress. Gene expression levels for drought tolerance and yield were validated by RT-qPCR and consistent with transcriptome analysis.

PI425425 (India), PI425045 (Philippines), PI425551 (Korea), PI264686 (Philippines), and PI425085 (Sri Lanka) were top five in the topsoil foraging ideotype. PI425594 (unknown origin), PI425599 (Thailand), PI425610 (Afghanistan), PI425485 (India), and AVMU0201 (Taiwan) were top five in the drought-tolerant and nutrient uptake steep, cheap, and deep ideotype.

Heterologous expression of PeNAC1 improves salt tolerance in transgenic oat. Overexpressing PeNAC1 increased (1,3;1,4)-beta-D-glucan content and expression of biosynthetic genes AsCslF3, AsCslF6, and AsCslF9 under salt stress, indicating PeNAC1 regulates (1,3;1,4)-beta-D-glucan synthesis. PeNAC1 is useful for improving oat salt tolerance and quality through molecular breeding.

A recombinant inbred line (RIL) population of 313 lines was derived from a cross between Longgu 3 and Canggu 3. The population was genotyped by whole-genome re-sequencing and phenotyped in four environments to detect the genetic basis of photoperiod sensitivity-related traits.

SbWRKY30 is a WRKY transcription factor in sorghum. SbWRKY30 is induced by drought stress. SbWRKY30 is expressed in sorghum taproot and leaf. SbWRKY30 has transcriptional activation activity and functions in the nucleus.

Illumina HiSeq 4000 sequencing was used to sequence the transcriptome of green-flower common buckwheat (Gr) with coarse pedicels and white-flower Ukrainian daliqiao (UD) with fine pedicels. 118,448 unigenes were obtained.

Several low-tannin foxtail millet varieties grown under Chinese chestnut trees attracted red spiders to feed on their leaves and protected the chestnut trees from infestation. The growth and yield of the foxtail millet plants were not greatly affected. To identify genes related to leaf tannin content and to select low-tannin foxtail millet germplasm for interplanting with Chinese chestnut to prevent red spider attack, leaves from 4 varieties with different tannin content levels were harvested for comparative transcriptome analysis.

Insertion and deletion (InDel)-based mapping detected QTLs qECL7.1 on chromosome 7 and qECL10.1 on chromosome 10. Substitution mapping with InDel, CAPS, dCAPS, and SNP markers narrowed qECL7.1 to a 418 kb region flanked by markers TC99_10,211,134 bp and TC102_10,628,880 bp.

RNA-seq and DAP-seq revealed that AWN1 is a transcriptional repressor. It bound directly to a motif in the regulatory regions of three MADS genes related to flower development and two genes, DL and LKS2, involved in awn development. AWN1 downregulates these genes, repressing awn elongation.
BSA-seq identified two major grain size QTLs on chromosomes 1 and 3. Fine mapping with SSR markers narrowed qGS1 to a 1.03 Mb region on chromosome 1.

Parents and RILs were genotyped with a 6K Illumina SNP array, generating 168 segregating SNPs. Seedling reactions to two Pca isolates (races TTTG, QTRG) were conditioned by two genes (0.6 cM apart) in this population.

Salt tolerance at germination and seedling stage of sorghum is a complex quantitative trait controlled by multiple genes. Six major QTLs and five chromosome regions are crucial for sorghum salt tolerance and can be applied in marker assisted selection.

A recombinant inbred line population was developed by crossing cultivar Yugu 5 and cultivar Jigu 31. The population segregated for hull color in a ratio of 2:1, indicating hull color is regulated by multiple genetic loci.

Transcription factors of the WRKY, MYB, and NAC families were involved in the response to salinity. WGCNA analysis identified stage-specific gene expression for salinity gradients in each cultivar. KEGG enrichment analysis explored gene function.

Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-induced drought stress affected seed germination, physiology, and biochemical mechanisms in 14 Tartary buckwheat genotypes. Four PEG stress conditions (0%, 10%, 20%, and 30%) were applied at the germination stage. Germination percentage, relative water content, and growth parameters differed significantly among the genotypes.
Three QTLs on chromosome 7H (QGpc.ZiSc-7H.1, QGpc.ZiSc-7H.2, QGpc.ZiSc-7H.3) were identified. Their genetic effects were validated using NILs.

GBS data with about 80-100 K SNPs is needed for accurate prediction of additive breeding values in tetraploid ryegrass. Using only SNPs with sequencing depth between 10 and 20 gave the highest predictive ability. This shows the potential for accurate prediction from medium-low coverage GBS in tetraploids.
Seita.9G321800 encodes the MYBS3 transcription factor. It showed upregulated expression after drought stress.
The predominant combinations in landraces were V1-8/V-2 and v(1)/V-2. The highest proportion in modern cultivars was v(1)/v(2). Haplotypes V1-5/v(2), V1-10/V-2 and V1-9/V-2 correlated with region.
Drought stress inhibits oat growth and yield. Fulvic acid (FA) improves oat drought resistance, but its molecular mechanism is unclear.

A high-density genetic linkage map was constructed with an average marker distance of 0.69 cM. Twenty-one QTLs were identified by composite interval mapping. One hundred sixteen candidate genes were predicted based on gene annotations and parental variations. Three genes were considered important candidates after integrating gene annotation, SNP and indel analysis, cis-element analysis, and expression patterns in varieties with different photoperiod sensitivities.

Expression levels of 53 key homologs involved in seed dormancy and germination regulation were changed. The 18 transcription factors and the homologs are potential candidates for ABA-mediated seed dormancy and germination regulation, and could be used for molecular breeding of quinoa elites with PHS tolerance.

QSc.VlWa.4H is the first major QTL for APR to scald on chromosome 4HS in barley. No known QTLs or genes are in a similar position. Combining the two QTLs provides stable scald resistance across four environments.

FtPMEI13 may inhibit the activity of FtPME44 and FtPME61, affecting pectin methylesterification and modulating stomatal closure under drought stress. The ABA-responsive transcription factor FtbZIP46 binds to the FtPMEI13 promoter, enhancing FtPMEI13 expression.
Most traits were controlled by one or two major QTLs, explaining 9.5-80.9% of phenotypic variation. Two dwarfing genes were identified from the cross.

One QTL on chromosome 4 and two QTLs on chromosome 7 were identified in the B140/CK60B population. They accounted for 17.9 to 24.9% of the phenotypic variance. The QTL on chromosome 4 was verified in another F-2 mapping population (MS138B/B140).

Pc98 was mapped using Kompetitive Allele-Specific PCR SNP markers. In the Pc98/Bingo mapping population, Pc98 is located on the Mrg20 linkage group and is bracketed by SNP markers GMI_ES22_c3052_382_kom399 and GMI_ES14_lrc18344_662_kom398 at genetic distances of 0.9 cM and 0.3 cM, respectively.

SbER10 and SbER4 are GENE members. SbER10 has three copies: SbER10_X1, SbER10_X2, and SbER10_X3. SbER4 has two copies: SbER4_X1 and SbER4_X2. SbER10 is located on CHR 10 of sorghum. SbER4 is located on CHR 4 of sorghum. SbER10 has high expression in pedicel tissue. SbER10 responds to treatment with abscisic acid, brassinolide, gibberellin, and indole-3-acetic acid.

Four genomic selection models (GBLUP, BRR, Bayesian LASSO, BayesB) were assessed for four sorghum grain antioxidant traits (phenols, flavonoids, total antioxidant capacity, condensed tannins) using whole-genome SNP markers. The models predicted performance for antioxidant production in new, unphenotyped sorghum genotypes. The study used a diversity panel of Sorghum bicolor lines and landraces and S. bicolor x S. halepense recombinant inbred lines.
The functional markers are tightly linked to the seed dormancy QTL. They may be used in marker-assisted selection for seed dormancy in sorghum.
Transgenic Arabidopsis seedlings showed higher tolerance to salt and osmotic stress than WT. Transgenic foxtail millet showed improved growth under salt and drought stresses compared with WT.

Sen consistently reduced photosynthetic functioning during heat shock. Tol increased its photosynthetic rate during heat shock. Higher abundance of heat shock protein transcripts and metabolites related to heat tolerance were noted for Tol compared to Sen, both before and during heat shock.

The bi17 marker is mapped to chromosome 18D. Dw6 was previously mapped to chromosome 18. The bi17 marker is diagnostic for Dw6 near-isogenic lines. This indicates the dwarfing gene in WAOAT2132 is Dw6.
Forty-seven QTLs were identified for straw weight, panicle weight, grain weight per plant and 1000-grain weight traits. These QTLs explained 5.5-14.7% of phenotypic variance.
In both RIPs, both parent lines contributed stay-green alleles. Three QTLs on linkage groups A, E and G were common to both RIPs for the stay-green trait, with alleles from E36-1.

An orthologous insect resistance gene Cysteine protease-Mir1 (XnhsbmSFC34/SBI-10) was significantly associated with major QTL for all traits except seedling vigor. It explained 22.1% of the phenotypic variation for deadhearts%, a measure of shoot fly resistance. Similarly, a NBS-LRR gene (XnhsbmSFCILP2/SBI-10) was associated with deadhearts% and number of eggs per plant.
Genic SSR markers were identified and used to detect polymorphism among 56 accessions. Population structure and genetic similarity coefficient were estimated.

The study identified major genomic regions for heat stress tolerance in chickpea. It used an integrated genomics-assisted breeding strategy. This strategy involved QTL-seq assay, association analysis and molecular haplotyping. It was deployed in a mapping population of 206 individuals and a diversity panel of 217 chickpea accessions.
Fe and Zn concentrations and 55,068 high-quality GBS SNP data from 140 sorghum accessions were used. Fe ranged from 22.09 to 52.55 ppm and Zn ranged from 17.92 to 43.16 ppm.

A genome-wide association study was performed on 428 spring oat lines using a high-density oat SNP array and a SNP-based consensus map. Marker-trait associations were performed using a Q-K mixed model approach.
Translocations from A- to C- and D- to C-genome chromosomes were less frequent. Rare translocations from A- to D-, D- to A- and C- to B-genome chromosomes were visualized.

A genetic linkage map of the B140/CK60B population was constructed with 216 SSR markers spanning 1710.3 cM. One QTL on chromosome 4 and two QTLs on chromosome 7 were identified. They accounted for 17.9 to 24.9% of the phenotypic variance.
Composite interval mapping identified 8 QTLs under normal conditions, 9 QTLs under drought, and 26 QTLs under salinity stress. Chromosomes 1, 4, 5, and 7 were important for salinity stress.

CARE analyses indicated numerous CAREs related to biotic and abiotic responses and hormone responses in FtNAC gene promoters. qRT-PCR showed tissue-specific expression and induction by PEG, NaCl, cold, MeJA, ABA, and GA treatments, implying abiotic and hormone responsiveness. FtNAC70 was the most strongly induced gene by all six treatments. FtNAC70-overexpressed Arabidopsis showed increased resistance to salt and drought.
The gibberellin 20-oxidase gene (HvGA20ox2) is the functional gene of the barley sdw1 mutants. Different deletions result in different functional alleles for different breeding purposes.
QTL mapping was conducted using unconditional and conditional methods. Candidate genes were predicted via transcriptome analysis of parental samples at three developmental stages.
PgNAC21 expression is induced by salinity stress and ABA treatment. The promoter contains ABA response elements (ABREs) and MYB TF binding sites.

Lines with Dw6 produced more productive tillers than lines without Dw6. The yield penalty associated with Dw6 might be partially due to the decrease of kernel weight, which is attributed to the reduction of kernel length.

Based on the stress tolerance index (STI), XiNong 9943, XiNong 9940, and QianKu-5 were tolerant, and QuanKu-4 was susceptible. These cultivars were selected for further characterization. Enzyme activity significantly increased with PEG dose.

The Casparian strip is key for root salt exclusion. The membrane domain protein (CASP) family participates in Casparian strip aggregation. The function and regulatory mechanisms of SbCASP in response to salt stress in sweet sorghum are unclear.

LCS177 and LCS234 exhibited high salt tolerance. LCS140 and LCS181 showed salt sensitivity. Under salt stress, proline, soluble protein, and soluble sugar contents increased more in salt-tolerant LCS177 and LCS234 than in salt-sensitive LCS140 and LCS181.

BADH plays an essential role in the salt-tolerance mechanism of quinoa. Based on its expression level and response to NaCl, BADH can be considered a molecular marker for screening salt-tolerant quinoa germplasm at early crop development stages.

The favorable alleles at these stable loci additively increased coleoptile length. Gene Ontology analysis of the candidate genes underlying the six stable QTLs revealed enrichment in cell development-related processes.
Two oat lines, Baiyan2 and Mengnongda1, were subjected to salinity stress (100 mM NaCl) for two weeks. Their growth and physiological parameters were compared.

SETIT_032906mg on chromosome 2 (5,020,600-5,029,771) is a homologous foxtail millet ortholog affecting target traits in rice. Markers cGWP6045 and kTGW2906 were developed for marker-assisted selection of foxtail millet with high grain weight.

The article summarizes the main breeding goals for sorghum and overviews essential genetic and genomic resources. It analyzes current and potential marker-assisted approaches in sorghum breeding. Advancements incorporate diverse methodologies beyond traditional techniques.

SSR41 and developed molecular markers were used to map the white leaf sheath gene SiWLS1. SiWLS1 encodes a chloroplast-localized protein. This protein regulates chloroplast development in bundle sheath cells of the leaf sheath in S. italica and is related to heavy metal sensitivity.

Wild-type HvVRN1 and the HvVRN1-8 allele are widespread. HvVRN1-1 & HvVRN1-8 are predominant in the Inner Mongolian Plateau spring barley region. HvVRN1-5 is predominant in the Northeast Plain spring barley region. Compared with landraces, the frequency of HvVRN1-8 decreased in commercial varieties. Wild-type HvVRN1 increased significantly (P < 0.01) in commercial varieties.

Association mapping was performed for panicle length, panicle width, panicle compactness, and peduncle recurving in sorghum using 6,094,317 SNP markers. One locus for recurving peduncles was mapped on chromosome 7 and one on chromosome 9. Eight loci were mapped for panicle length, panicle width, and panicle compactness.
Tartary buckwheat (Fagopyrum tataricum) is a crop with nutritional value and drought resilience. Drought after flowering reduces yield.

Under moderate stress, JIA2 upregulated 1086 genes and downregulated 2919 genes. Under severe stress, JIA2 upregulated 1792 genes and downregulated 4729 genes. Under moderate stress, BA9 upregulated 395 genes and downregulated 669 genes. Under severe stress, BA9 upregulated 886 genes and downregulated 439 genes.
Sixteen ABI5 genes were identified in foxtail millet. Their sequence composition, gene structures, cis-acting elements, chromosome positions, and gene replication events were analyzed.

Differences among the significantly associated SNPs were observed in environments under different temperatures. The 65 SNP markers can be used in cowpea molecular breeding to select drought tolerant phenotypes through marker assisted selection.
SiLTP-OE lines performed better under salt and drought stresses than WT plants. RNAi lines were more sensitive to salt and drought than WT.

It retained high biomass production and a high tolerance index. It had a low threshold of fraction of transpirable soil water and high capacity to recover leaf apparatus after drought stress. The expression levels of four genes indicated they could be used as a proxy for drought tolerance.

The BMX-08010-2 genotype showed significant regression coefficient more than unity and non-significant deviation from regression values, indicating suitability for favorable environments for grain yield. Based on stability, additive main effects, and multiplicative interactions analysis, BMX-010015 and BMX-08010-2 are suitable for tolerance to water deficit stress.

Multi-environment QTL mapping identified 23 stable loci and 34 co-located QTL clusters for panicle architecture and grain yield-related traits. These provide a genetic basis for foxtail millet yield improvement. Panicle architecture and grain weight affect grain yield potential. Both are influenced by genetic and environmental factors.

Forty-seven marker-trait associations were detected under drought-stressed conditions, and one under non-stressed conditions. The candidate genes and markers are useful for accelerated groundnut breeding targeting drought tolerance.

Four resistance loci on chromosomes 3, 6, 8 and 9 were identified against Puerto Rico pathotypes. Two resistance loci on chromosomes 3 and 8 were identified against Texas pathotypes. In Georgia and Florida, three resistance loci were detected on chromosomes 4, 5, 6 and four on chromosomes 4, 5 (two loci) and 7, respectively.

Tartary buckwheat (Fagopyrum tataricum) exhibits strong tolerance to environmental stresses. The FtMYB9 gene, encoding an R2R3-MYB transcription factor, was studied. FtMYB9 expression was induced by ABA, cold, salt, and drought treatments in the seedling stage.

Transcriptome analysis of leaf samples from water-controlled sorghum seedlings was performed. Treatments: normal water supply (70% soil water content, CK), mild drought (50%, DR1), and severe drought (30%, DR2).
Pollination methods affected seed set in autotetraploid S4 lines. Differences in seed set among lines indicate selection of lines with high seed set and use for hybrid production.

The study aimed to identify molecular markers linked to ergot resistance and pollen traits (pollen quantity and pollen viability) in sorghum. It also aimed to assess the relationship between these pollen traits and ergot resistance. A genetic linkage map was constructed for the sorghum RIL population R931945-2-2 x 8525 using 303 markers, including 36 SSR, 117 AFLP, 148 DArT, and two morphological trait loci.
Twenty-seven SSR markers were used for 20 mungbean genotypes. Twenty-one genic SSR markers showed polymorphism, alleles ranged from two to six, average PIC value was 0.34.

Targeted deep sequencing analyzed frequencies of small insertions and deletions induced by sgRNAs targeting four endogenous sorghum genes. Indels were induced in sorghum protoplasts at frequencies up to 77.8% (plasmid) and 18.5% (RNP).

Two BAC libraries were constructed from cultivar Vada and line SusPtrit. Vada is immune to non-adapted Puccinia rust fungi and partially resistant to P. hordei. SusPtrit is susceptible to several non-adapted rust fungi and has been used for mapping QTLs for non-host and partial resistance.

The map segments of Ftq1 and Prq1 and of Ftq7 and Prq7 overlap. This suggests linkage between the flowering time QTLs and resistance QTLs or a pleiotropic effect of the Ftq QTLs on rust resistance. Partial resistance to crown rust in the field has low heritability (0.30), indicating potential value for marker-assisted selection.

Quantitative trait loci (QTLs) and genes affecting seed dormancy in sorghum are largely unknown. To identify genomic regions controlling seed dormancy, we produced two F-2 segregating populations from crosses between a deep dormant weedy line B140 (female parent) and two weak dormant grain lines CK60B and MS138B (male parents).
Differentially expressed genes analysis showed 7320 genes responded to drought stress. Of these, 2671 genes had opposite expression trends before and after rewatering.

The oat genome identified 194 AsaPP2C genes. These genes are unevenly distributed across all 21 chromosomes. Phylogenetic analysis classified the PP2C genes into 13 subfamilies (A-L). Each subfamily has conserved motif compositions and exon-intron structures.

26,549 microsatellite markers were designed from flanking sequences of 37,572 microsatellites. 2,643 (9.96%) were genic microsatellite markers. All markers were physically anchored to the eight chromosomes of F. tataricum. A high-density physical map was constructed with an average marker density of 58.82 markers per Mb.

Overexpressing FlbZIP12 in Tartary buckwheat root hairs promoted drought tolerance. It increased superoxide dismutase and catalase activities, decreased malondialdehyde content, and upregulated stress-related gene expression. FlbZIP12 overexpression also induced the expression of key flavonoid biosynthesis genes.

Drought caused ascorbic acid and total phenolic content to decrease, and total flavonoid content to increase in all cultivars/lines. It also significantly reduced N, P, K, Ca and Mg, but Fe remained unchanged in all cultivars/lines.

Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) has tolerance to cold, drought, and salinity but is sensitive to high temperature. A metabolomic and transcriptome study of cultivars Dianli-3101 and Dianli-3051 under high temperature stress detected 794 metabolites and 54,200 genes. Photosynthesis-related genes were down-regulated. Lipids and flavonoids showed the largest changes in accumulation.

The RR genotypes had higher grain yield, harvest index, and water use efficiency for grain than the ER genotypes under rainfed and irrigated conditions, and under drought and well-watered conditions in the rainout shelter. Aboveground biomass and harvest index had significant direct effects on grain yield. Leaf dry weight was negatively associated with grain yield in the rainout shelter.

Thirteen PLD genes were identified in sorghum. They were divided into 7 groups based on phylogenetic analysis. All sorghum PLD family members contained two conserved catalytic domains, HDK1 and HDK2. Most members also contained a C2 domain.

80 candidate gene-based markers were developed, targeting seven shoot fly resistance genomic regions. Of 17 polymorphic candidate genes, seven genes were significantly associated with 18 major QTL for component traits of resistance in multiple QTL mapping, and two genes in single-marker analysis.

SiMBR2 transcription is induced by salicylic acid, gibberellic acid, salt, and osmotic stresses. High or low temperatures decrease its transcription. Heterologous expression of SiMBR2 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhances tolerance to water deficit by reducing reactive oxygen species accumulation under drought stress.

Untargeted metabolic analysis identified 523, 406, 301 and 272 differential metabolites in L1 and HZ1 on day 3 and day 9 of drought stress. Key metabolites (amino acids, nucleotides, peptides, organic acids, lipids, carbohydrates) accumulated differently in quinoa leaves. HZ1 had the most DEMs in Glycerophospholipid metabolism (ko00564) and ABC transporters (ko02010) pathways.
A genetic linkage map was constructed using SSR markers. Stable QTLs were identified for six drought tolerance traits under irrigation and drought treatments.

To monitor gene expression changes under drought during the reproductive stage in barley leaves, the 22K Affymetrix Barley 1 microarray screened two drought-tolerant genotypes Martin and HS41-1, and the drought-sensitive genotype Moroc9-75. Seventeen genes were expressed exclusively in the two drought-tolerant genotypes under drought stress. Their encoded proteins may enhance drought tolerance through controlling stomatal closure via NADP-ME and PDH, synthesizing osmoprotectant glycine-betaine via CSMO, generating protectants against reactive-oxygen-species via ALDH and ADOR, and stabilizing membranes and proteins via HSP17.8 and DHN3.

We compile recent progress using physiological and molecular approaches, discuss sorghum's responses to different stresses, and summarize candidate genes involved in regulating abiotic stresses. We also exemplify differences between combined and single stresses, emphasizing the need to study molecular responses to combined abiotic stresses.

A single major quantitative trait locus for flowering time under short-day conditions (DTF3A) was mapped to a 59-gene interval on chromosome three containing a cluster of three FT genes. The genes collectively showed upregulated expression in domesticated relative to wild parent lines. An equally strong association with growth habit suggests a pleiotropic effect of the region on both traits.

Using composite interval mapping and an RFLP map spanning 1,355 cM with 144 loci, nine QTLs for stay green were detected across seven linkage groups in several environments. Three QTLs on linkage groups A, G, and J were consistent with published results.

Two major QTLs, qSPAD-7-1 for SPAD value and qTric-7-2 for trichome density, were identified on chromosome 7 in mungbean using recombinant inbred line (RIL) populations from the cross PMR1xPusa Baisakhi. Functional analysis identified 35 candidate genes in the QTL region: 16 for SPAD value and 19 for trichome traits.
PsPP2C67 and PsPP2C82 are clade A PP2C genes and were highly induced under high salinity stress at early stages. They are involved in ABA-related processes.

Combined analysis of DEGs and DEMs in hormone synthesis found AUX/IAA, SAUR, CRE1, A-ARR, PP2C, and SNRK2 genes, and 3-indoleacetic acid and jasmonic acid were differentially expressed among different salt concentrations. The study compared two genotypes of brewing sorghum for gene and metabolite expression differences in response to salt stress.
The study included 1,515 F2 tetraploid ryegrass families. Phenotypes and genotypes were scored on family-pools for the traits dry matter yield (DM), rust resistance (RUST), and heading date (HD).

We identified 46 drought-responsive candidate genes by performing a machine learning-based transcriptome study on two drought-tolerant and two drought-sensitive foxtail millet cultivars. We screened 12 important drought-responsive genes by principal component analysis and confirmed them experimentally by qPCR.

We identified DE-mRNAs and non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) involved in phenylpropanoid biosynthesis and plant hormone networks. A ceRNA-miRNA-target gene network was generated. circRNA_2746, circRNA_6515, circRNA_5622, XR_002450182.1, XR_002452422.1, XR_002448510.1, XR_002448296.1, LOC8056546, LOC8062245, LOC8061469, and LOC8071960 are candidates for regulating GA(3)-mediated salt stress alleviation in sorghum.

Association analysis using SNPs from the pan-genome identified 398 SNPs significantly associated with agronomic traits, including 92 in genes. Drought gene expression analysis identified 1,788 genes linked to different conditions, with 79 absent from the reference genome.

The study identified stable shoot fly resistant genotypes among 385 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) from a cross between a susceptible parent and a resistant parent. The RILs were evaluated in eight environments over three years for shoot fly resistance and component traits.

Four novel xiaomi-like mutants, xiaomi3, xiaomi4, xiaomi5, and xiaomi6, were identified. The mutants exhibited an extremely early heading phenotype, heading 30-40 days after sowing under natural long-day conditions. The mutants showed reduced plant height, leaf length, leaf width, panicle length, and panicle diameter compared to their wild-types.

Previous research identified an association between virulence to Pc45 and the crown rust resistance gene PcKM in the varieties 'Kame' and 'Morton'. This study aimed to reveal the relationship between Pc45 and PcKM.
Marker-trait associations were identified on chromosomes 1, 3, and 5. SNPs S01_72265728 and S05_58213541 explained 35% and 32% of Fe and Zn variance, respectively.

Twelve key differentially accumulated metabolites (DAMs) and ten key candidate DEGs involved in drought response were identified. The DAMs are D-galactose, UDP-glucose, succinate, inositol, D-fructose-6-phosphate, D-glucose-6-phosphate, D-glucose-1-phosphate, dihydroxyacetone phosphate, ribulose-5-phosphate, citric acid and L-malate. The DEGs are CqAGAL2, CqINV, CqFrK7, CqCELB, Cqbg1x, CqFBP, CqALDO, CqPGM, CqIDH3, and CqSDH. CqSDH, CqAGAL2, and Cq beta-GAL13 were validated in transcriptomics and a yeast expression screen system.

Overexpression of the AsCDPK26 gene enhanced salt resistance in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. AsCDPK26 correlated with Na+/H+ antiporter 1, suggesting it may interact with an ion transporter to modulate salt resistance.

Cd stress was analyzed in cultivated buckwheat (Pinku-1, K33) and perennial species (F. tatari-cymosum Q.F. Chen, DK19) at two critical periods: days 7 and 14 after treatment. Cd stress led to changes in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the chlorophyll system. Cd-response genes related to stress response, amino acid metabolism, and ROS scavenging were enriched or activated in DK19.

In the 35 S:SbCASP-LP1C1-GFP lines, the expression levels of the genes MYB36 and ESB1 were increased. SbCASP-LP1C1 may be involved in lignin monomer polymerization in the Casparian strip of sweet sorghum, thereby regulating salt tolerance.

Three elite lines with improved malting quality and agronomic traits were selected as a parental line to incorporate a wild barley allele for breeding a commercial variety. A new strategy uses marker-assisted selection and backcrossing to transfer a favorable allele from a wild parent.

RNA-seq data showed lower expression of beta-amylase 2 in YG than in An. Expression levels of three SWEET genes and four PIP genes were higher in YG than in An, allocating more photosynthetic sugar to the roots.
FLOWER LOCUS-like (FTL) and Phytochrome A (PHY A) may interact with SiCO, SiCOL1, and SiCOL6. SiCO, SiCOL1, and SiCOL6 are involved in flowering and heading in foxtail millet.

A synonymous SNP at 558 bp (A/G) in the SiDREB2 gene of foxtail millet (Setaria italica L.) is associated with dehydration tolerance. An allele-specific marker (ASM) was developed. The ASM was validated in 170 foxtail millet accessions using single-marker regression analysis.

Salt-treated Baiyan2 retained similar root potassium (K+) levels compared to control plants, indicating Baiyan2 maintains ionic homeostasis in root tissues under saline conditions. Salt-treated Mengnongdal seedlings showed a 34.3% reduction in root K+.

23 VrBBX genes were identified. They were named based on their physical locations on chromosomes. All VrBBXs were divided into five groups based on phylogenetic relationships, B-box number, and presence of a CCT domain. Homology and collinearity analysis indicated BBX genes in mung bean and other species underwent conservative evolution.

In silico analysis showed Shaker K+ channel gene expression was tissue or developmental stage specific. qRT-PCR detected transcription levels of Shaker K+ channel genes in foxtail millet under abiotic stresses (cold, heat, NaCl, PEG) and phytohormones (6-BA, BR, MJ, IAA, NAA, GA3, SA, ABA) treatments at 0, 12, and 24 h.

The pg mutant is deficient in Chl b because its gene product converts Chl a to Chl b. The independent Chl b-less mutant line M4437_2 carries a nonsynonymous substitution (F263L) in the C domain of HvCAO.

We identified 333 NAC genes from the common oat genome. The overview covers gene structure, chromosomal localization, phylogenetic characteristics, conserved motif compositions, and gene duplications.

Basal soil Zn fertilization increased the flavonoid content of foxtail millet by up-regulating genes related to flavonoid metabolism and biosynthesis, including flavanone-3-hydroxylase, chalcone isomerase, and leucoanthocyanidin reductase. Foliar Zn application enhanced flavonoid content by up-regulating genes involved in flavonoid metabolic and biosynthetic processes and chalcone isomerase.

Lentil rust caused by fungus Uromyces viciae fabae is a serious lentil disease in Algeria, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, India, Italy, Morocco, Pakistan and Nepal. Symptoms occur during flowering and early podding stages.

Salt-tolerant proso millet (ST 47) had better salt tolerance, biomass accumulation, and osmo-protection than salt-sensitive proso millet (SS 212). ST 47 maintained better internal surfaces and intact structures to resist Na+ toxicity and maintain optimal growth.

Common buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum) is a crop with gluten-free grains and high phenolic compounds. Buckwheat yields are affected by high water requirements during grain filling. Karst lands are a poor substrate for plant growth due to low nutrients and water content.

Drought stress affected energy dissipation and antioxidant enzyme system in sweet sorghum inbred lines M-81E and Roma. Under rehydration, the germination indicator increased more in M-81E than in Roma.

LRNK1 had significantly higher plant height, leaf area, and chlorophyll contents than LR2381. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) analysis showed that plant hormone signal transduction, carbohydrate catabolic processes, and photosynthesis were the main pathways responding to salt stress in sorghum.

Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses were performed on oat plants treated with or without silicon and inoculated with Pga. Silicon treatment increased the activities of catalase, peroxidase, and superoxide dismutase under Pga infection, inhibiting reactive oxygen species accumulation.

Soil-borne barley yellow mosaic virus disease is caused by strains of Barley yellow mosaic virus and Barley mild mosaic virus. Winter barley is affected by this disease. The recessive resistance gene rym11 is on chromosome 4HL and is effective against strains of BaMMV and BaYMV.

Root apex tissue studies showed increased malate exudation in the Al-tolerant parent UFRGS17, but not in the sensitive parent. The malate transporter is a candidate gene for one of the Al tolerance QTLs identified.

Half of the tillering QTL co-located with QTL for component traits. Tillering QTL and candidate gene locations coincided across populations. Common non-synonymous SNPs were identified in the parental genotypes of two mapping populations in a sorghum homologue of MAX1, a gene controlling tiller bud outgrowth through strigolactone production.

A study on marker-assisted selection (MAS) for the rf1 gene was conducted on the offspring of crosses between maintainer line BTx-622 and sweet sorghum lines BJ-299 and Lunen-2. The simple sequence repeat marker Xtxp18 showed high accuracy for selecting recessive homozygotes for the rf1 gene.

Two QTLs conferred male-sterility on chromosome 6: qSiMS6.1 with a major effect and qSiMS6.2 with a minor effect. Both QTLs exhibited complete dominance. The major QTL, qSiMS6.1, was delimited to a 186-kb interval between the markers SiM20 and SiM9 by joint analysis of QTL-seq and QTL mapping with SSR and structure variation markers.

The salt tolerance of oat cultivars was highest in BY953, followed by Keyan1, BY896, and BY898. Under salt stress, BY953 had higher chlorophyll content, soluble sugar, protein levels, K+/Na+ ratio, and antioxidant enzyme activity than BY898. BY898 had higher proline concentration. BY953 responded earlier to salt stress via proline metabolism, peroxisome, and ion transport pathways.
Five chromosome regions controlled multiple traits under salt stress. Salt tolerance at germination and seedling stage in sorghum is a complex quantitative trait controlled by multiple genes.
OsOAT expression was induced by drought via ABA-dependent and ABA-independent pathways. Overexpression of OsOAT in rice enhanced drought and osmotic stress tolerance.

We mapped 12 QTL for seedling drought tolerance and maturity in a cowpea RIL population from a cross between VAR IT93K503-1 and VAR CB46. The 127 F-8 RILs were screened with 62 EcoR1 and Mse1 primer combinations, generating 306 AFLP MRK for genetic linkage mapping.

SiYTH1 formed dynamic liquid-like cytosol condensates under drought stress. SiYTH1 is a cytoplasmic protein and an m(6) A reader. It stabilizes SiARDP and ROS scavenging-related transcripts under drought stress.

We detected 32,170 expressed genes and characterized 13,552 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) correlated with drought treatment. Most DEGs were identified in root tissue, then leaf and stem tissues. The number of DEGs in stems of drought-sensitive cultivars was about two times higher than in drought-tolerant cultivars.

GWAS-derived markers had better prediction accuracy than genome-wide markers. Plant height had the highest prediction rate with 100 GWAS-derived markers, while other traits required more markers. This advances genomic prediction in small oat breeding programs by optimizing prediction rates and reducing marker numbers, confirming high rates are achievable with smaller datasets.
Silencing SiGSTU18 decreased catalase activity and proline content, leading to elevated hydrogen peroxide levels. This increased malondialdehyde content and inhibited plant growth.
Candidate gene prediction revealed ten uncharacterized genes. Seven genes possess NB-ARC domains. qPCR analysis revealed SbiRTX2783.06G018400 is the most likely candidate for aphid resistance.

A major quantitative trait locus (QTL), Chalk5, influences grain chalkiness, head rice yield, and other quality traits. Chalk5 encodes a vacuolar H(+)-translocating pyrophosphatase (V-PPase) with PPi hydrolysis and H(+)-translocating activity.

Under alkali stress, the Fv/Fm, ETH, Phi PSII, and chlorophyll content of sorghum variety Z14 were significantly higher than those of variety Z1. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) increased in both varieties. The enzyme activities of SOD, POD, CAT, and APX increased significantly, especially in Z14, resulting in lower ROS compared to Z1.

QSc/Sl.cib-7H exhibited pleiotropic effects on plant height, thousand grain weight and grain length. It did not significantly influence spikelet number of main spike and grain width. Transcriptome analysis showed regulation of SC and SL might be related to the plant circadian rhythm pathway.

Evaluation of marker genotypes in crown rust differential lines supported Pc91 as the identity of QPc.CORE.18.3. SNPs with rare alleles associated with lower disease scores may be suitable for marker-assisted selection of oat lines for crown rust resistance.

After 20% PEG treatment, 119 differentially accumulated metabolites were identified in stems and 188 in leaves. Accumulations of soluble sugars (raffinose, trehalose, glucose, sucrose, melibiose) and amino acids (proline, leucine, valine, serine, arginine) were significantly increased. Transcriptome sequencing identified 1711 and 4978 DEGs in stems, and 2061 and 6596 DEGs in leaves after 6 and 48 h of 20% PEG treatment. Expressions of genes involved in sucrose biosynthesis (SUS1, SUS2), trehalose biosynthesis (TPS6), raffinose biosynthesis (RAFS2, GOLS2), proline biosynthesis (P5CS2, P5CR), leucine and valine biosynthesis (BCAT2), and arginine biosynthesis (ASS, ASL) were significantly upregulated.

A high-density consensus genetic map was developed with 7,876 molecular markers. It anchored 43 QTLs and 7 genes for scald resistance from different mapping populations. QSc.VlWa.4H is a major QTL for adult plant resistance to scald on chromosome 4HS in barley, with no known QTLs or genes reported in a similar position.
The SNPs were used in GWAS with mrMLM software. 42 SNPs were associated with five forage quality traits.

Ten MQTL with physical intervals under 1 Mb and seven hotspot regions with a high QTL-overview index were identified for drought tolerance and yield maintenance in foxtail millet. This study identifies QTNs associated with phenotypic variation for traits in sorghum. Traits include days to flowering (101 days), days to maturity (145.77 days), plant height (357.47 cm), seed number per plant (1808.92 count), seed yield (45.07 g), and thousand-seed weight (23.44 g).

GWAS identified 81 marker-trait associations for ten traits. High confidence associations were identified for three agronomic traits: flag leaf width, grain yield, and thousand-grain weight.
Nineteen QTL were identified for leaf width, adjusted for flowering time. These QTL correspond to those in maize and rice.

We used these viruses to deliver sgRNAs to Cas9 and GFP transgenic sorghum lines, targeting Phytoene desaturase (PDS), Magnesium-chelatase subunit I (MgCh), 4-hydroxy-3-methylbut-2-enyl diphosphate reductase, and orthologs of maize Lemon white1 (Lw1) or GFP.
The study aimed to identify QTL for salt tolerance in wild zombi pea (Vigna vexillata) accession AusTRCF 322105. A BC1F2 population from cross TVNu240 x AusTRCF 322105 was used for QTL analysis.

SbWRKY50 is required for lateral root development in Sorghum bicolor. Overexpression of SbWRKY50 increased lateral root number and length. The CRISPR/Cas9-edited SbWRKY50 mutant decreased lateral root number and length.

Methods: We conducted image-based phenotyping on 369 accessions from the sorghum Bioenergy Association Panel (BAP) in a controlled environment with early cold treatment. Linkage analysis showed that Blp1 co-segregated with HZSNP34 and HZSNP36. More polymorphic markers were screened in the target region and used to genotype the population.

The SiABI5s promoter contains cis-acting elements for hormone and stress responses. The expression of 16 genes was analyzed in tissues, seed germination, and ear development.

The study improved terminal drought tolerance in pearl millet hybrid HHB 226 by introgressing drought tolerance QTLs from 863 B into the male parent HBL 11 of the hybrid. Marker-assisted foreground selection used four polymorphic SSR primers on linkage group 2 and 5 to identify plants with resistance alleles in the BC4F2 population.

A recombinant inbred line population was developed by crossing ZAU 7 to ND16092. A linkage map of 111 molecular markers was constructed. Simple interval mapping was performed to identify QTL for plant height in eight environments.

Plants were exposed to heat stress (35/30°C day/night) or drought stress for 21 days. RNA-seq transcriptomic profiling in A. stolonifera (cv. 'Penncross') found 670 commonly up-regulated and 812 commonly down-regulated genes under heat and drought stress.

Sorghum seeds discolor during storage. Citric acid treatment improves sensory quality and antioxidant activity. This study compared phenotypic and antioxidant activity between citric acid-treated and water-treated sorghum seeds.

RNA-Seq compared transcriptome profiles determining GCA for yield-related traits between barley genotypes Baodamai 12 and Ximala 22. 1051 differentially expressed unigenes (DEGs) were found, with 599 up-regulated and 452 down-regulated.
Twenty mungbean genotypes were evaluated for powdery mildew severity. Eight genotypes (500167, LM 19, MN 98, V2540, V2564, VC1210A, VC6468-11-1A) were resistant with significantly lower AUDPC.
Qingyongjiu 195 enhances K+ uptake via KAT1 and AKT2, and sequesters Na+ in vacuoles via NHX2. It involves DEGs in photosynthesis (chlG, CP47 psbB, COX2, LHCB) and antioxidants (trxA, GroES).

Genome-wide association mapping identified loci for morphological and yield traits in buckwheat. Genotyping by sequencing identified 34,978 single nucleotide polymorphisms distributed across eight chromosomes.

Four QTLs explained 86.3% to 48.9% of the additive genetic variance for basal tillers with heads. Seven QTLs explained 85.9% to 47.9% of the additive genetic variance for panicle width. Five QTLs explained 65.8% to 52.0% of the additive genetic variance for main-culm height.

A cross between the resistant sorghum accession PI 607900 and the susceptible elite cultivar BTx623 produced an F-2 mapping population of 371 individuals. This population was tested for resistance to greenbug biotype I in the greenhouse.

Gene expression analysis and RNA-Sequencing confirmed activation of citrulline biosynthesis-related genes OTC, AOD, and CPS, and down-regulation of catabolic genes ASL and ASS in drought-stressed leaf tissues. The nitrogen status of the plant regulates citrulline, based on relative abundance in nitrogen-depleted vegetative tissues and down-regulation of citrulline biosynthesis genes.

We identified 47 ERF genes from the adzuki bean genome. Transcriptome analysis under saline-alkaline stress showed that 13 ERF genes were induced.

The elite TB inbred line Guiku1 has a telomere-to-telomere gap-free genome assembly. The Guiku1 genome spans 453.83 Mb and contains 43,441 predicted protein-coding genes. An ethyl-methyl-sulfonate-induced mutation library with rich phenotypes was also presented.

A genome-wide association study (GWAS) identified genomic regions controlling TKW in oats. A panel of 383 oat genotypes, adapted to subtropical conditions, was evaluated in three environments to elucidate the genetic architecture of TKW.

Recombinant inbred lines (RILs) showed variation in yield, grain number per square meter, time to anthesis, plant height, CGR, P-R and E-G. The study assessed agronomic traits and their correlation with yield in 32 quinoa varieties. Yield categories were low (<= 1500 kg ha(-1)), middle (1500-2500 kg ha(-1)), and high (>2500 kg ha(-1)).

Other QTLs are associated with these traits. Some QTLs are environment-specific. For tillering, QTL analysis and transcriptomics identified 6189 differentially expressed genes during tiller bud elongation.

The BC1F2 population was subjected to a hydroponic condition with 250 mM NaCl to evaluate salt tolerance at the seedling stage by assessing plant leaf wilt and plant survival. QTL analysis revealed that two QTLs, qSaltol_3.1 and qSaltol_7.1, control leaf wilt and plant survival.
Chickpea experiences severe yield loss during heat stress. Understanding the genetic architecture regulating heat stress tolerance is important for enhancing yield under heat stress.

QTL analysis revealed five QTL pairs regulating FLL and FLW. SqFLL-6H.2 & SqFLW-6H.1 and SqFLL-7H.1 & SqFLW-7H.1 were co-localized major QTLs stably detected in multiple environments, named SqFLS-6H and SqFLS-7H, with average PVE of 14.07% and 21.96%, respectively.

We used two recombinant inbred line (RIL) populations from crosses between cold-tolerant (CT19, ICSV700) and cold-sensitive (TX430, M81E) parents. The RIL populations were evaluated for SNP using GBS in field and controlled environments for chilling stress response.

SbCASP-LP1C1 was localized in the plasma membrane of sweet sorghum root endodermal cells. Its function was studied by heterologous expression in Arabidopsis (35 S:SbCASP-LP1C1-GFP). When germinated on 50 mM NaCl, the SbCASP-LP1C1-expressing lines had longer roots and a higher salinity threshold compared with wild-type (Col-0) and the casp-lp T-DNA insertion mutant in Arabidopsis.
Six Tartary buckwheat cultivars were used: short-stemmed XQ1 and CQ1, mid-length stemmed YQ1 and QK3, and tall-stemmed DAB and DN1. The stem characteristics differed significantly among these types.

Genetic analysis identified a monogenic dominant dwarfing gene from WAOAT2132, designated DwWA. An existing SSR marker (AME117) and a new codominant PCR-based marker (bi17) developed in this study were both associated with DwWA. The markers were located 21 and 1.2 cM from DwWA, respectively.

CqCBL10 and CqNHX4 contributed to salt stress resistance. In combination with Cqtrihelix23, they synergistically enhanced salt stress tolerance.
MSG26 was mapped to a 0.02-cM region between markers SP1M14 and SP1M49. The candidate gene HORVU4Hr1G074840 encodes a cytochrome P450 protein (CYP704B).

Thirty-four tillering QTL were identified across populations, of which 15 were novel. The QTL analysis suggested that the contribution of traits associated with S/D balance or PTT to genotypic differences in tillering differed among populations.

The F-2 population from this cross was used to map the rust resistance gene using SSR and SRAP markers. 270 SRAP and 162 SSR markers were studied; 101 SRAP and 33 SSR markers were polymorphic between the parents.

A linkage map was constructed with 104 marker loci, including 50 EST-SSRs, 34 non-genic nuclear SSRs, and 20 SNPs. QTL analysis was performed using composite interval mapping. Eight QTLs were mapped for root traits and 20 QTLs for yield traits.

A large set of highly polymorphic SSR markers were developed based on genomic sequence comparison between different Setaria genotypes. The new SSR markers are placed on the physical map and represent a resource for diversity studies, genetic map construction, functional gene mapping, QTL exploration and molecular breeding in foxtail millet and related species.

Genes for the pink stem and petiole mutant trait and flavonoid content variation were identified using forward- and reverse-genetics approaches. The T2T gap-free genome of Guiku1 and its EMS mutation library provide resources for functional genomics and genetic improvement.

To identify genes for resistance to powdery mildew, 696 barley accessions were evaluated for PM resistance at seedling and adult growth stages. Using the FarmCPU model, 54 markers showed significant associations with PM resistance at seedling and adult-plant stages.

Under PEG-induced water stress, NM5 maintained stable gene expression levels. Compared with drought-sensitive cultivars, the different regulation strategies in the JA signal transduction pathway in drought-tolerant cultivars may be a driving force for drought stress tolerance.

The genetics of lentil winter hardiness was studied by QTL analysis to identify markers for marker-assisted selection. 106 recombinant inbred lines from the cross WA8649090/Precoz were evaluated for winter survival.

Four Tartary buckwheat genotypes were used to investigate the high NH4+ response mechanism. The root and shoot growth of Tartary buckwheat seedlings were inhibited by 50 and 100 mmol/L NH4+ treatments.
Two QTL were found on chromosomes 3C (Mrg17) and 18D (Mrg04). These QTL are associated with BYDV tolerance.

The transcription levels of Shaker K+ channel genes SiAKT1, SiKAT3, SiGORK, and SiSKOR in foxtail millet were detected by qRT-PCR under cold, heat, NaCl, PEG, 6-BA, BR, MJ, IAA, NAA, GA3, SA, and ABA treatments at 0, 12, and 24 h. Genotyping-by-sequencing SNP markers linked to Pg2 were identified in an AC Morgan/CDC Morrison recombinant inbred line population. The Pg2-linked SNPs were analyzed in an AC Morgan/RL815 F-2 population and an AC Morgan/CDC Dancer recombinant inbred line population.
