PHL, Y(II), qP, DTRBA, SSCL, 0-60 cm IPAR, and k in the 0-30 cm layer correlated significantly with yield.
SiCBL4 and SiCIPK24 were identified and characterized for salt stress tolerance in foxtail millet. Both genes were induced by salt, ABA, MV, and heat shock stress in seedlings.

DArT markers distributed across the chickpea genome were used to determine population structure. An admixture model in STRUCTURE identified three sub-populations. Pairwise linkage disequilibrium (LD) estimated using squared-allele frequency correlations (r² < 0.20) decayed rapidly at a genetic distance of 5 cM.
Sorghum has high salt tolerance. A F-2 segregating population and bulked segregation analysis (BSA) sequencing were used to locate sorghum salt tolerance genes.

Lipid transfer proteins (VrLTPs) were induced under high-salt conditions. They were co-expressed with transcription factors WRKY, MYB, and NAC. VrLTPs function as regulators of late-stage stress adaptation. VrLTPs are salt-induced transcriptional hubs. They have a critical role in mung bean's adaptation under high salinity.

The study determined if dormancy QTLs are related to PHS. PHS was measured as sprout score (SSc) from mist chamber-treated spikes and as alpha-amylase activity (AA) in kernels from spikes with little visible sprouting.

SiARDP constitutive expression in Arabidopsis thaliana enhanced drought and salt tolerance during seed germination and seedling development. SiARDP overexpression in foxtail millet improved drought tolerance. SiARDP target gene expression levels were upregulated in transgenic Arabidopsis and foxtail millet.

The study achieved transformation and gene editing efficiencies of ~70% and up to 17.5% in two sorghum genotypes. Analysis of homozygous E-0 lines in the E-1 generation confirmed stable mutation integration for all targeted genes.

We identified 26 Meta-QTLs in sorghum. The average confidence interval of Meta-QTLs was refined 2.56-fold compared to initial QTLs. This identified known functional genes and novel candidate genes for the traits.

Oat (Avena sativa L.) breeders select the thousand kernel weight trait (TKW) to increase grain yield and quality. Genomic regions controlling TKW in oats, especially in subtropical environments, need better understanding.
Plant height is a GCA-sensitive trait important for biomass production. Female lines AMP418, AMP431, AMP434, AMP443, AMP495, AMP496 and male line X097 were selected as high-GCA effect germplasm.

The races TJD, TJN, and TKN were used to evaluate resistance in 30 Chinese oat cultivars at seedling and adult plant stages. Cultivars Bayan 1, Baiyan 2, Baiyan serving 5, and Baiyan 9 were highly resistant to those races.

The GCA effect on grain yield was positively correlated with productive tiller rate, AGBY, and harvest index. The GCA effect on AGBY was positively correlated with plant height, gravity center height, productive tiller rate, and days to maturity, but negatively correlated with 100-grain weight and grain width.
The gene SiTGW6 governs grain yield in foxtail millet. SiTGW6 encodes an IAA-glucose hydrolase, localized in the cytoplasm and expressed in flowering panicles.
The parents were surveyed for RFLPs at 84 marker loci covering about 1100 cM of the barley genome. The RFLP genotypes of the F(1)s were deduced from the parents.

In a previous study, SiMBR2 (Seita.7G226600), a gene linked to drought stress, was identified. Ten SiMBR genes were identified in foxtail millet. Their structural characteristics, chromosomal locations, promoter cis-acting regulatory elements, and tissue- or developmental stage-specific transcription patterns were analyzed.

A population of 190 recombinant inbred lines derived from the cross between Chinese landrace ZGMLEL with high grain protein content and Australian cultivar Schooner was used for linkage and QTL analyses. Grain protein content was evaluated under six environments for the RIL population and the parental lines.

QTLs for number of stem nodes (qNSN) and stem juice weight (qSJW) were detected on Chr 6, with PVE values of 17.63% and 37.68%, respectively. The QTL for panicle neck length (qPNL) was located on Chr 3 and explained 14.25% of the phenotype variation.
The HvGLR3.5 gene was analyzed. Three mutations were identified by screening 2000 M-2 lines. Two mutations displayed tuft and yellow striped leaves compared to the wild type.

The genetic linkage map included 159 SSR markers and 37 Indel markers. QTL mapping used this map and phenotypic data of nine panicle-related traits in F2:3 families. It identified 22 QTL with phenotypic variation explained (PVE) of 0.06-50.14%.

In WGCNA, the dark green module (7082 genes) positively correlated with CC. The black module (1393 genes) negatively correlated with CC and RWC. The module positively correlated with CC highlighted ribosome synthesis and plant hormone signaling.

Pm41 was mapped in a 0.6 cM interval flanked by markers XWGGC1505 and XWGGC1507. The XWGGC1506 marker co-segregated with Pm41 and can be used for chromosome landing, map-based cloning, and marker-assisted selection of Pm41.

Based on ASV indices, varietal stability rankings were PS5 > YS13 > JS8 > PS3 > PS6 > PM4 > others. GGE analysis indicated PM4 had broad adaptability across environments, while JS15 exhibited specific adaptability in Datong.

There were reports of additional loci controlling caryopsis adherence in cultivated barley. The origin of naked genotype is not conclusive. A newly developed marker was applied to screen the nud locus among 1291 globally-collected barley accessions. The genotyping result coincided with the caryopsis phenotype.

Four stable stay-green QTLs (StgB, Stg1, Stg3, Stg4) were introgressed from donor parent B35 into senescent variety R 16 using partial introgression (BC2F3/BC1F4 generations). The introgression lines were evaluated in well-watered and post-flowering stress environments. Compared to R 16, most lines had higher leaf chlorophyll levels at flowering and greater percentage green leaf area during late grain filling, indicating phenotypic expression of the stay-green QTLs in the R 16 background.
Four markers were located on Mrg21 between 194.0 and 205.7 cM. Two markers mapped to Mrg05 and Mrg09. Three SNPs associated with lemma color were located on Mrg17, Mrg18, and Mrg20.
Subcellular localization assay showed SiHXK5 and SiHXK6 were localized in mitochondria. Haplotype analysis revealed SiHXK3-H1 was associated with higher plant height and grain yield.

A field experiment with spring wheat (Triticum aestivum), hulless oats (Avena nuda), and hulled oats (Avena sativa) was conducted to determine crop responses to nitrogen addition. Biomass, nitrogen, and phosphorus accumulation and partitioning were examined during the growth season.

SiCDPK7 in foxtail millet responds to heat and cold stress. Over-expression of SiCDPK7 in Arabidopsis confers heat stress tolerance by increasing seedling survival rates and hypocotyl elongation compared to wild type plants. It also enhances heat stress tolerance in foxtail millet.
A QTL for plant height is on chromosome 7HL. This QTL is not associated with maturity or rachis internode length. Its provisional name is Qph-7H.
OsOAT-overexpressing plants showed increased tolerance to oxidative stress. Glutathione content and ROS-scavenging enzyme activity were increased in these plants.
VrbZIP and VabZIP gene expression profiles responded to drought, salt, and ABA stress. These results provide gene expression evidence for selecting candidate genes under drought and salt stress.
Samples were genotyped using 48 K SNP markers. Phenotypic data on 17 traits was collected and analyzed.

The field experiment showed genetic variation in oat germplasm resources. The correlation analysis showed that biological yield was positively correlated with the D-value. Eighteen high-quality, high-yielding, saline-alkali-tolerant oat germplasm resources were identified. These 18 saline-alkali-tolerant germplasms provide resources and a basis for saline oat cultivation and saline-tolerant breeding.

Polymorphic markers were incorporated onto the AFLP map and analyzed for association with drought response QTL using JoinMap 3.0 and MapQTL 4.0. Seven markers co-located with previously identified QTL peaks. Isolation, sequencing, and blast analysis confirmed their homology with drought or abiotic stress-induced ESTs from cowpea and other plants.
Composite interval mapping identified 91 QTL for 11 traits, with 5-12 QTL per trait. Each QTL explained 2.5-30.3% phenotypic variation. Six major genomic regions had QTL effects on multiple traits.

The study investigated two oat varieties: high β-glucan variety BY and low β-glucan variety DY. It examined β-glucan content during different filling stages. β-glucan accumulation was highest from days 6 to 16 of filling. Transcriptome sequencing of seeds was performed at different filling stages.

The section examines drought impact on sorghum production, pre-breeding and breeding of sorghum, and opportunities for breeding early-maturing, high-yielding, and water-use-efficient sorghum varieties. It outlines opportunities and challenges of breeding methods for developing climate-smart, early-maturing, and drought-tolerant sorghum varieties.

Ectopic expression of FtWRKY46 enhances Arabidopsis tolerance to salt stress. Transgenic plants expressing FtWRKY46 have higher seed germination rate, root length, chlorophyll content and proline content than WT plants under salt stress. They also have lower MDA levels than WT plants.

The awn1 gene encodes a transcription factor with an ALOG domain. awn1 is responsible for awn loss during sorghum domestication. awn1 arose from a gene duplication on chromosome 10 and translocated to chromosome 3. awn1 acquired high expression after duplication and represses awn elongation in domesticated sorghum. Comparative mapping revealed high collinearity at the awn1 paralog locus on chromosome 10 across cereals. Inactivating the rice awn1 ortholog reactivated awn growth and development on the rice spikelet.

Na2CO3 stress inhibited plant height, root length, stem diameter, total root volume, and total root surface area of oat seedlings. The inhibition increased with higher alkali stress concentrations. Peroxidase (POD), superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT) activities and malondialdehyde (MDA) content in oat seedling leaves increased with increasing alkali concentrations.
The F1 generation of sorghum hybrids displayed heterosis during anthesis. P-n at anthesis serves as an indicator for predicting yield potential and screening carbon-efficient varieties.

Two major MTAs were identified on chromosome arms 3HS and 5HL. The MTA on 3HS contributed to adult plant resistance. The MTA on 5HL contributed to seedling and adult plant resistance. An MTA on 7HS contributed mainly to adult-plant resistance. An MTA on chromosome arm 1HS made a significant contribution to seedling resistance.
A 10 μM Cd concentration was used for analyses. 2683 genes and 160 metabolites had significant differential abundances between the control and Cd-treated groups.

Natural variations in the SiPLATZ12 promoter affect SiPLATZ12 expression and salt tolerance between millet (Hap1 genotype) and wild ancestors (Hap18 genotype). The expression levels of SiNHX1, SiNHX2, SiNHX3, and SiNHX7 correlate with the salt tolerance of Hap1 and Hap18 millet seedlings.

PDH1 transcript levels showed the opposite trend compared to proline content in seeds stored 12 months. PDH1 maintained lower levels in seeds at 16% and 28% moisture content. P5CS1 transcript level was significantly affected by moisture content. PDH1 could improve stress resistance for seed aging and maintain seed vigor during long-term storage.

Some major QTLs were identified on chromosomes 2, 3, 4, 7 and 9: for peduncle number per plant (qPeN2.2), pod length (qPoL3), seed breadth (qSB4), seed length (qSL7.2) and seed thickness (qST9). Previously reported QTLs for pod length (qPoL8) and 100-seed weight (qSW8) on chromosome 8, and for seed number per pod (qSN9.2) on chromosome 9 were confirmed. These QTLs are useful for marker-assisted selection.

Eight models of haplotype changes in domestication genes from wild sorghum to landraces and improved sorghum were observed. Sh1 and SbTB1 genes represent two models: soft selection or multiple origins, and hard selection or an early single domestication event. The Dry gene, which regulates stem juiciness, was unconsciously selected during grain sorghum improvement.

The genes were unevenly distributed on nine foxtail millet chromosomes. Chromosomes 2, 3, and 9 contained the most SiCDPK members. Most foxtail millet CDPK genes contained the ABRE, LTR, HSE, MYB, MYC, DRE, CGTCA-motif, and TGACG-motif cis-acting elements. These elements can be activated by abiotic stresses.

Barley is categorized as hulled or naked based on caryopsis adherence. Hulled barley is used for animal feed and brewing, while naked barley is consumed by humans. The naked trait is controlled by a 17-kb deletion containing the entire ERF gene on the nud locus on barley chromosome 7HL.

Sequencing of the two offspring pools identified 903,025 SNP and 438,453 InDel variants. Genome-wide screening found 163 polymorphic loci with SNP-index values near 0.75 in the salt-tolerant pool and 0.25 in the non-salt-tolerant pool.

Cultivar Brisasul and cultivar UPFA Gauderia have higher beta-glucan content. Cultivar URS 21 and cultivar URS 22 have higher protein content. Cultivar Barbarasul and cultivar FAPA Louise have high lipid content.
733 primers produced reproducible and polymorphic amplicons among 28 Setaria genotypes. These SSR markers detected 2 to 16 alleles with an average polymorphism information content of 0.67.

Genome-wide association studies using 26,196 SNPs identified 34 SNPs, representing 32 QTLs significantly associated with coleoptile length. Six of these QTLs were consistently detected in both experiments, explaining 6.43% to 10.07% of the phenotypic variation.

The dwarfing gene from TX9425 is located at a position similar to the uzu gene. It differs from the uzu gene by being temperature sensitive and closely linked to short spikes, awns, and high grain density, resembling a brh gene.

QTL for seed weight and days to flowering in mungbean were identified. The mapping population of 155 F-2 lines was derived from a cross between Kamphaeng Saen 1 (large-seeded, early flowering) and V4718 (small-seeded, late flowering).

We studied rust resistance inheritance in lentil using F-1, F-2, and F-2:3 populations from the cross PL 8 (susceptible VAR) x L 4149 (resistant VAR). Genetic analysis showed that a single dominant gene controls rust resistance in lentil genotype L 4149.

Transcriptome and metabolome association analysis showed that gene-LOC110713661 and gene-LOC110738152 may be key genes for drought tolerance in quinoa. Metabolites accumulated in quinoa leaves under drought stress, and plants recovered after rewatering.
GSHO745' is a spontaneous male-sterile mutant from the barley variety Unitan'. The male sterility in GSHO745' is controlled by the recessive gene msg26.
We identified 30 HAK genes (CqHAK1-CqHAK30) in quinoa. They are distributed across 18 chromosomes.

HD-related genes expression varied with TOS. Eleven of fourteen QTL aligned with HD gene positions. Three new QTL included one at 73.5cM on chromosome 2H, explaining 19.2% and 4.6% HD of DH lines in spring and summer.

GWAS using BLINK identified significant loci for drought tolerance in cowpea. A cluster of 196 SNPs on chromosome 5 was associated with tolerance to trifoliate leaf chlorosis under drought stress. A GWAS peak on chromosome 1 was associated with tolerance to unifoliate leaf chlorosis under drought stress. 25 SNPs on chromosomes 1, 3, 5, and 11 were associated with plant greenness under drought stress.

The stress-associated protein (SAP) gene family member SbSAP14 from Sorghum bicolor has A20 and AN1 zinc-finger domains. SbSAP14 expression is induced by dehydration, salt, oxidative stress, and abscisic acid treatment.
Phospholipase D (PLD) is involved in drought tolerance. The full-length cDNA of PLD alpha 1 was cloned from foxtail millet.

Sorghum bicolor is an important cereal crop. Its growth and distribution are limited by alkali conditions. Alkaline-sensitive Z1 and alkaline-tolerant Z14 sorghum genotypes were used as experimental materials to study alkali effects on sorghum seedlings.
qRT-PCR analysis revealed that VrKNAT7-1 and VrCYP86A expression in seed coat of ACC41 is higher than KPS2. VrKNAT7-1 controls seed dormancy in ACC41.

The AsSnRK2D protein and its 12 and 21 counterparts were classified into Group II and SnRK2a, respectively. The AsSnRK2D gene was constitutively expressed and responded positively to abscisic acid, low-temperature, salt, and dehydration stress. The AsSnRK2.7 protein was localized primarily in the nucleus.

These mutants displayed diverse panicle architectures and hull colors. Under controlled short-day and long-day conditions, the mutants showed an early heading phenotype. Mutations in the Phytochrome C (SiPHYC) gene, including transposon insertions and a frame shift mutation, caused the early heading phenotype.

High NH4+ down-regulated most DEGs involved in antioxidant enzyme system, hormone signaling, and N transport and assimilation. Co-expression analysis suggested possible hub genes for regulating high NH4+ response, including FtNRT1.14, FtMYB61/52, FtbZIP6/34, FtNAC72/73, and FtLTP14.
The yeast complementation assay verified the inward K+ transport activities of Shaker K+ channels. SiKAT2 interacts with SiSNARE proteins.

Marker-assisted selection based on significant loci from linkage disequilibrium studies can be used in sorghum breeding for antioxidant production. This work conducted a genome-wide association study of sorghum grain antioxidants using single nucleotide polymorphisms in a diversity panel of Sorghum bicolor landraces and S. bicolor x S. halepense recombinant inbred lines.

Comparative genomics analysis of markers flanking the Pm41 locus in wheat and orthologous genes in Brachypodium, rice, and sorghum shows that gene order is highly conserved between rice and sorghum. However, intra-chromosome inversions and re-arrangements are evident in wheat and Brachypodium genomic regions. Gene duplications are present in the orthologous genomic regions of Pm41 in wheat, indicating that the Brachypodium gene model provides useful information for wheat marker development.

RAD-seq generated a high-density genetic map for foxtail millet. 9,968 SNP markers genotyped 124 F-2 progenies from a cross between Hongmiaozhangu and Changnong35. The map spanned 1648.8 cM with an average distance of媽 of 0.17 cM. 11 major QTLs for eight agronomic traits were identified. Five co-dominant DNA markers were developed.

Candidate genes were mined by analyzing gene variants and expression patterns in the target region using genome and transcriptome data. This study advances the cloning of QSc/Sl.cib-7H. The data and developed molecular markers will facilitate its use in barley breeding.

140 sorghum accessions, including broomcorn (72), half-broomcorn (4), and non-broomcorn (64), were genotyped using 45 SSR markers. The broomcorn accessions had average N-A of 9.09, PIC of 0.60, and H-e of 0.63. These values were higher than those of half-broomcorn (N-A 2.64, PIC 0.46, H-e 0.52) but lower than those of non-broomcorn (N-A 11.69, PIC 0.73, H-e 0.75).

186 SSR markers were assigned to 18 linkage groups corresponding to the haploid chromosomes. The map length was 3033.42 cM, covering 78.17% of the reference genome. The 18 linkage groups ranged from 88.89 cM.

The study investigated the root transcriptomic response of foxtail millet to the plant elicitor peptide 1 (Pep1). Transcriptome analysis identified 401 differentially expressed genes in Pep1-treated roots.

A genetic map was generated in a population of 158 F-6-derived oat recombinant inbred lines from a cross of partial resistance line MN841801-1 by susceptible cultivar selection 'Noble-2'. The map was developed to detect quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for partial resistance to oat crown rust, Puccinia coronata f. sp. avenae Eriks. It used 230 marker loci, mostly restriction fragment length polymorphism and amplified fragment length polymorphism markers. The map spanned 1,509 cM (Haldane) arranged into 30 linkage groups of 2-18 markers each.

The map contained 3129 Bin markers from 48,790 SNPs spanning 1460.996cM. Fifty-seven QTLs for 11 agronomic traits were detected using composite interval mapping, with phenotypic variation explained of 0.38-30.52%.

A high-density genetic linkage map of the powdery mildew resistance gene Pm41 was constructed. Pm41 originates from wild emmer (Triticum turgidum var. dicoccoides) and was previously mapped to chromosome 3BL bin 0.63-1.00. The map used an F-5:6 recombinant inbred line population from a cross of durum wheat cultivar Langdon and wild emmer accession IW2. Comparative genomics analyses developed 19 polymorphic sequence-tagged site markers, which were integrated into the Pm41 map.

CqHAK1, CqHAK13, CqHAK19, and CqHAK20 were induced in leaves under high saline condition. CqHAK1, CqHAK13, CqHAK19, and CqHAK20 were induced in leaves under alkaline condition. CqHAK6, CqHAK9, CqHAK13, CqHAK23, and CqHAK29 were induced in roots under alkaline condition.

The Dirigent (DIR) gene family is important for lignin polymerization and stress adaptation in plants. Its characterization in Sorghum bicolor is underexplored. Using the S. bicolor genome database, we performed genome-wide identification, phylogenetic classification, and expression profiling of the DIR gene family.

Sweet sorghum is a bioenergy crop and forage. A sweet sorghum cultivar showed physiological responses to PEG-induced osmotic stresses. Metabolome profiling after 20% PEG treatment analyzed differentially accumulated soluble sugars and amino acids. Transcriptome sequencing identified key genes involved in the biosynthesis pathways of soluble sugars and amino acids.
Busseola fusca and Chilo partellus are insect pests of sorghum. They can cause 15% to 80% grain yield loss.

Buckwheat (Fagopyrum tataricum) is a crop. We analyzed morphophysiological indicators and metabolomes of two drought-tolerant buckwheat varieties under drought treatments to explore the drought stress resistance mechanism.

A total of 22 SiFKBPs and 26 SiCYPs genes were identified in the Setaria italica genome. Phylogenetic analysis showed that FKBP and CYP proteins from Setaria italica and other plant species clustered into nine distinct groups.
BADH was more sensitive to salt stress and played an important role in quinoa seedling salt stress tolerance. It showed upregulation until 24 h under 100 mM NaCl and until 12 h under 250 mM NaCl.

A wild population of drought-tolerant Fagopyrum leptopodum has potential for enhancing drought tolerance in cultivated buckwheat. The expression of gene FlbZIP12 from F. leptopodum is induced by abiotic stresses including abscisic acid, salt, and polyethylene glycol.

The newly-developed microsatellite markers were evaluated with 440 randomly selected markers in F. tataricum. The markers showed high amplification efficiency and are valuable. The large number of new microsatellite markers and their location on the physical map provide a resource for studying diversity, constructing genetic maps, functional gene mapping, QTL exploration and molecular breeding in Fagopyrum species.

DArT markers associated with barley GPC were detected by GWAS. GWAS revealed two HvNAM genes as candidate genes controlling GPC. No association was detected between HvNAM1 polymorphism and GPC. A SNP (798, P < 0.01) located within the second intron of HvNAM2 was associated with GPC.

Bioinformatics analysis showed that glutathione metabolism (GSTU6, GSTU1, GSTF1), amino acid biosynthesis (ArgB, GS, hisC, POX1), and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis (HST, C3 ' H) pathways were enriched in GA2 and LG31. Co-expression analysis indicated that GA2 had enhanced atrazine tolerance due to improved glutathione metabolism and proline biosynthesis. Scopoletin enrichment may help LG31 resist atrazine stress.
The Chl a and Chl b contents in sbgpgl1 were lower than in BTx623. The net photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, and transpiration rate were reduced in sbgpgl1 compared to BTx623.
In the zeta subfamily, the C2 domain was replaced by PX and PH domains. The exon-intron structure of SbPLD genes within the same subfamily was highly conserved.
